title: India Tells Nationals in Saudi Arabia to Stay Alert After Houthi Missile Strikes
excerpt: The advisory followed Houthi-claimed ballistic missile attacks on Riyadh and Abha airports; Air India, IndiGo, Air India Express and Akasa cancelled Riyadh flights until October 10.
body:
• India has advised its nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain alert and vigilant after Yemen's Houthis claimed ballistic missile strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
  • The Indian Embassy in Riyadh issued the advisory Thursday evening; the Ministry of External Affairs condemned the targeting of civilian infrastructure at Abha and Riyadh airports as "completely unacceptable," noting civilian deaths and injuries.
  • Air India, IndiGo, Air India Express and Akasa Air cancelled Riyadh flights until October 10, with one Delhi–Riyadh flight turning back mid-way; Lufthansa Group suspended Riyadh flights through October 16.
  • What it means for you: about 2.75 million Indians live in Saudi Arabia — follow only official advisories, do not record or circulate videos of the incidents, and check with your airline before travelling; full refunds and free rescheduling are being offered.

India on Thursday advised its nationals in Saudi Arabia to stay alert and follow local authorities' instructions, after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The advisory landed as airlines cancelled Riyadh flights and the Ministry of External Affairs condemned the attacks on civilian infrastructure.

The attacks

The Houthis claimed responsibility for a ballistic missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Thursday, and issued renewed threats against airlines after claiming the attack, according to Reuters. Smoke was seen rising from a stationary aircraft at the airport, according to a witness and three people briefed on the matter. Saudi Arabia's Abha airport also came under attack in recent days, as escalation between the Iran-backed Houthi group and Saudi Arabia intensified with armed-drone and missile strikes.

India's advisory

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh issued an "IMPORTANT ADVISORY" on X on Thursday evening. Its full text: "In view of the current situation, all Indian nationals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia are advised to remain alert and vigilant, stay indoors as necessary, and follow the instructions issued by local authorities through official channels. Indian nationals are strongly advised to refrain from circulating or reposting any videos or news related to the ongoing events."

The embassy's warning not to record or circulate videos carries extra weight amid reports of a Saudi crackdown on such footage — a sensitivity sharpened by earlier attacks on hotels in the early phase of the Iran war.

MEA condemns the strikes

The Ministry of External Affairs condemned the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport, which resulted in civilian deaths and injuries. "The targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable. We express our deepest condolences to the families of those who have lost their loved ones. We wish speedy recovery for those injured. We express solidarity and stand with the people and government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," the ministry said.

Flights disrupted

The disruption to air travel was immediate. Air India cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh until October 10; flight AI2243 from Delhi to Riyadh returned mid-way to Delhi and was subsequently cancelled. Passengers are being offered full refunds. Air India operates seven weekly flights to Riyadh from Delhi and Mumbai.

Air India Express cancelled its Riyadh flights until October 10 as well — 16 weekly flights from Bengaluru, Kochi, Kannur and Kozhikode — offering affected guests complimentary rescheduling or a full refund. IndiGo cancelled its Riyadh flights until October 10, and Akasa Air cancelled Thursday's QP 523 (Kochi–Riyadh) and QP 524 (Riyadh–Kochi), citing the evolving security situation. Lufthansa Group went further, suspending flights to Riyadh through October 16 due to "current developments in the Middle East," a spokesperson told Reuters.

What comes next

Approximately 27.48 lakh — about 2.75 million — Indian nationals reside in Saudi Arabia, according to a Ministry of External Affairs annexure tabled in the Rajya Sabha this year, making this one of the largest Indian communities abroad. With the Houthi–Saudi escalation continuing, the embassy's advisory is likely to remain in force; Indians in the Kingdom should monitor the Indian Embassy in Riyadh's official channels, avoid circulating unverified footage, and confirm flight status with airlines before heading to the airport.
